module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 760

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/760](https://www.erdosproblems.com/760)
- [AKS97] Alon, Noga and Krivelevich, Michael and Sudakov, Benny, *Subgraphs with a large
  cochromatic number*. J. Graph Theory (1997), 295-297.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos760

/--
The cochromatic number of $G$, denoted by $\zeta(G)$, is the minimum number of colours needed to
colour the vertices of $G$ such that each colour class induces either a complete graph or
independent set.

If $G$ is a graph with chromatic number $\chi(G)=m$ then must $G$ contain a subgraph $H$ with
$$
\zeta(H) \gg \frac{m}{\log m}?
$$

A problem of Erdős and Gimbel, who proved that there must exist a subgraph $H$ with
$$
\zeta(H) \gg \left(\frac{m}{\log m}\right)^{1/2}.
$$
The proposed bound would be best possible, as shown by taking $G$ to be a complete graph.

The answer is yes, proved by Alon, Krivelevich, and Sudakov.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos760.lean"]
theorem erdos_760 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (m : ℕ),
      G.chromaticNumber = (m : ℕ∞) →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, ∃ k : ℕ, ((k : ℕ∞) ≤ H.coe.cochromaticNumber) ∧
          (c * (m : ℝ) / Real.log (m : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
A problem of Erdős and Gimbel, who proved that there must exist a subgraph $H$ with
$$
\zeta(H) \gg \left(\frac{m}{\log m}\right)^{1/2}.
$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_760.variants.erdos_gimbel :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (m : ℕ),
      G.chromaticNumber = (m : ℕ∞) →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, ∃ k : ℕ, ((k : ℕ∞) ≤ H.coe.cochromaticNumber) ∧
          (c * Real.sqrt ((m : ℝ) / Real.log (m : ℝ)) ≤ (k : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos760

reformulations.difference: The lower bound is expressed using a natural-number witness k satisfying k ≤ ζ(H) and c·m/log(m) ≤ k, rather than comparing directly with ζ(H). The statement also includes m=0 and m=1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite H, its cochromatic number is a finite natural number z. Existence of such a k is equivalent to c·m/log(m) ≤ z: one direction follows by transitivity, and the other takes k=z. At m=0 or m=1, Lean's logarithm/division conventions make the lower bound zero, so H=⊥ and k=0 suffice. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, main_reformulation proves the equivalence with the direct cochromatic-number bound restricted to m≥2, without using the problem theorem.

reformulations.difference: The square-root bound likewise uses an auxiliary natural k below ζ(H) and includes m=0,1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Finiteness makes ζ(H) a natural number z, so ∃ k≤z with c·sqrt(m/log(m))≤k is equivalent to the direct bound c·sqrt(m/log(m))≤z. At m=0,1 the square-root expression is zero, making these additional cases automatic. The equivalence with the direct bound for m≥2 is proved as variant_reformulation in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov, Subgraphs with a Large Cochromatic Number (1997), complete paper, especially §1, Theorem 1.1 and the following sharpness remark: https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/PDFS/cochrom2.pdf

Benny Sudakov's publication list, entry for the cited paper: https://people.math.ethz.ch/~sudakovb/papers.html

review.notes:
Both declarations match the cited primary paper. Its introduction explicitly restricts graphs to finite simple graphs, records the Erdős–Gimbel square-root bound, and states their conjecture that the square root can be omitted. Theorem 1.1 proves the stronger asymptotic bound (1/4+o(1))m/log₂(m). Changing logarithm base only changes the positive constant; finitely many small positive cases can also be absorbed into that constant. Thus answer(True) and both research solved tags are supported.

Independent Lean checks verified finiteness of the cochromatic number, empty/nonempty boundary behavior, positivity of the bounds for m≥2, and executable small coloring cases. The cited external proof contains no placeholders or custom axioms. After proof-only compatibility changes from its stated v4.29.1 environment to the installed v4.33.1, its unchanged mathematical theorem compiled with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Its partition definition was also proved equivalent to Cocolorable.

The live https://www.erdosproblems.com/760 page returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers. Its current webpage remarks could not be read; the mathematical and solved-status checks instead use the cited primary paper. All experiments and the compatibility port are under /workspace/review; no repository files were edited.
